MUQATIL:63:9-11/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:63:9-11/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:63:9-11/r2.claim: Before death, hypocrites should spend their wealth; at death one asks for a short delay to give alms and obey God's commands.

MUQATIL:63:9-11/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:63:9-11/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:63:9-11/r3.claim: Aṣṣaddaq means purify my wealth by almsgiving; being among the righteous means being among believers, as in 9:75.

FARRA:v3p159/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p159/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p159/r4.claim: وأكن is jussive by returning to the conditional verb as if the ف in فأصدق were absent; Abdullah's reading وأكون returns to the overt verb and is accusative.

FARRA:v3p159/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p159/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p159/r5.claim: The common accusative is allowed even without written واو because Arabic sometimes omits that letter, as in manuscript spellings such as سليمن and فقلا.

TAB-FULL:v22p671/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p671/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p671/r1.claim: Believers should spend before death; the dying person asks for a brief reprieve to give alms and obey God by fulfilling obligations.

TAB-FULL:v22p671/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p671/r2.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v22p671/r2.claim: Another interpretation of becoming righteous is to perform the pilgrimage to the Sacred House.

TAB-FULL:v22p671/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p671/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p671/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a person who dies without paying zakat or performing Hajj asks to return; he reads “give alms” as zakat and “be righteous” as Hajj.

TAB-FULL:v22p671/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p671/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p671/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Hajj is due when one has a mount to carry them and provisions to get there.

TAB-FULL:v22p673/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p673/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v22p673/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk describes a believer dying with wealth but unpaid zakat, unperformed Hajj, and unpaid dues to God; he asks to return, but death is not delayed.

TAB-FULL:v22p673/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p673/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p673/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās similarly says such a believer asks to return in order to give charity and zakat before the appointed death.

TAB-FULL:v22p673/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p673/r3.speaker: سفيان
TAB-FULL:v22p673/r3.claim: Sufyān glosses the requested alms and righteousness as zakat and Hajj.

TAB-FULL:v22p673/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p673/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p673/r4.claim: Most regional readers recite wa-akun with jussive mood, coordinated with the implied jussive after fa-asaddaq; Ibn Muḥayṣin and Abū ʿAmr read wa-akūna in the subjunctive, coordinated with the subjunctive fa-asaddaq. Both readings are valid.

ZAJJAJ:v5p177/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p177/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p177/r3.claim: Tafsīr says anyone who neglected zakat or pilgrimage asks for another chance when facing death.

ZAJJAJ:v5p177/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p177/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p177/r4.claim: The reading fa-aṣṣaddaq wa-akun makes the first verb a response to lawlā (“if only you delayed me”); akūn is jussive by coordination with that response’s syntactic position and conditional sense.

ZAJJAJ:v5p177/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p177/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p177/r5.claim: The reading fa-aṣṣaddaq wa-akūna follows the overt form of the first verb, with both verbs in the same mood.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p635/r12.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p635/r12.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p635/r12.claim: These readers use jazm in وأكن and omit its wāw; Abū ʿAmr reads وأكون with wāw.

NAHHAS:v4p436/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p436/r1.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v4p436/r1.claim: The wording indicates that what God calls provision is lawful provision.

NAHHAS:v4p436/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p436/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p436/r10.claim: Aṣaddaq derives from ataṣaddaq, with tāʾ assimilated into ṣād because they are close within one word.

NAHHAS:v4p436/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p436/r11.speaker: الضحاك
NAHHAS:v4p436/r11.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports Ibn ʿAbbās's reading wa-azakkā.

NAHHAS:v4p436/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p436/r12.speaker: غيره
NAHHAS:v4p436/r12.claim: Another explanation says being righteous means performing obligations and avoiding prohibitions, that is, being righteous among the righteous.

NAHHAS:v4p436/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p436/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p436/r2.claim: Fa-aṣṣaddaq is the response to the wish introduced by laula.

NAHHAS:v4p436/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p436/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p436/r3.claim: Wa-akun is coordinated to the position before fa, not to the words after it; Arabic often coordinates to underlying position.

NAHHAS:v4p436/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p436/r4.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v4p436/r4.claim: Al-Hasan, Ibn Muḥayṣin, and Abū ʿAmr read wa-akūna in the accusative; a similar reading is attributed to Ubayy and Ibn Masʿūd, but it differs from the canonical written text.

NAHHAS:v4p436/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p436/r5.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v4p436/r5.claim: He rejects an appeal to the spelling of kalimn, since Qur'anic analogues yakūnu, takūnu, and nakūnu retain wāw.

NAHHAS:v4p436/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p436/r6.speaker: غيره
NAHHAS:v4p436/r6.claim: Another grammarian says the wāw in kalimn was omitted because it was already represented in the preceding spelling sequence; ordinary speech needs no such device.

NAHHAS:v4p436/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p436/r7.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v4p436/r7.claim: Sibawayh says without fa the verb would be jussive as a response to a question carrying a wish; poetry illustrates it.

NAHHAS:v4p436/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p436/r8.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v4p436/r8.claim: He cites a poem as evidence for coordination to underlying syntactic position.

NAHHAS:v4p436/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p436/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p436/r9.claim: The Qur'anic wa-yadharhum may be jussive on the position after fa, or nominative by following the overt form.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p293/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p293/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p293/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr alone reads وأكون with wāw; he coordinates the verb with the visible, subjunctive form فأصدق.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p293/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p293/r2.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p293/r2.claim: The other readers read وأكن without wāw, coordinating it with فأصدق's underlying jussive position as the response to an implied condition.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p293/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p293/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p293/r3.claim: Both syntactic attachments are defensible: one follows the underlying jussive position and the other the expressed wording; the verse means, 'Delay me and I will give charity.'

THALABI:v9p323/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p323/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p323/r2.claim: The particle la in the dying person's plea may be extra, expressing a wish, or may mean 'why not?' as a question.

THALABI:v9p323/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p323/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p323/r3.claim: The person's request to give charity means giving zakat; 'being among the righteous' means believers according to Muqatil and other commentators.

THALABI:v9p323/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p323/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p323/r4.claim: Another view says the righteous here are pilgrims and that the verse concerns believers rather than hypocrites.

THALABI:v9p323/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p323/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v9p323/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says a person who dies with wealth but unpaid zakat, or who could afford pilgrimage but omitted it, asks at death to return and give charity, meaning to perform Hajj.

THALABI:v9p323/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p323/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p323/r6.claim: Abu Amr and Ibn Muhaysin read 'wa-akūna' with a waw and subjunctive nūn as a response to the wish or question; Abu Amr says the codex omitted the waw for brevity.

THALABI:v9p323/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p323/r7.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v9p323/r7.claim: Al-Farra cites codices of Abd Allah and Ubayy with 'wa-akūna' and a waw as support for that reading.

THALABI:v9p324/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p324/r1.speaker: أبو عبيد
THALABI:v9p324/r1.claim: Abu Ubayd prefers the jussive 'wa-akun' because it is in Uthman's codex, used by most readers, and grammatically coordinates with the underlying position of 'fa-asaddaq'; an old poetic line illustrates this.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r5.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r5.claim: The commanded spending is obligatory alms due on wealth.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r6.claim: Alternatively, it is voluntary charity, aid for the needy, and help for the distressed.

QUSHAYRI:v3p321/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p321/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p321/r14.claim: Do not trust safe circumstances; expect death suddenly, prepare to depart, and do not persist in procrastination.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p477/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p477/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p477/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says spending from what God provided means paying the wealth's alms.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p477/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p477/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p477/r6.claim: Abu Ishaq says the warning urges continuous remembrance and generosity before death makes the person certain of what is coming and asking to be delayed.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p477/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p477/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p477/r7.claim: The dying person asks for a short extension of his term so that he can give alms and pay zakat.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r1.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r1.claim: Ata transmits Ibn Abbas's argument that these people were not believers, since a believer does not ask to return to life; only an unbeliever does.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r10.claim: A further poetic example carries the clause forward according to the position after a suppressed فاء.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r11.claim: Abu Amr's وأكون follows the spoken surface rather than the underlying meaning, which the author considers preferable because it is more explicit and closer in wording.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r2.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says anyone dying without pilgrimage or alms asks for another chance, and he reads وأكن من الصالحين as pilgrimage.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas defended his reading that being among the righteous means making pilgrimage by reciting the verse and saying أحج.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r4.claim: Abu Ishaq explains the plea as would that You delay me.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r5.claim: The jussive reading وأكن follows the syntactic position of فأصدق as a conditional response, while وأكون follows the surface wording.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r6.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r6.claim: Al-Mubarrad says وأكون follows the preceding wording because فأصدق answers a wish expressed by لولا أخرتني, while the jussive follows the underlying position that would occur without the فاء.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r7.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r7.claim: Abu Ali explains the jussive as coordinated with the position of فأصدق: postponement is an implied condition, as in أخرني أصدق.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r8.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r8.claim: Sibawayh's poetic examples illustrate grammatical government by an expression's underlying syntactic position; one example has نصب الحديدا after the position of بالجبال.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r9.speaker: لبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p478/r9.claim: Labid's line likewise places معدا in the accusative according to the underlying position, because من is treated as extra.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:63:9-11/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:63:9-11/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:63:9-11/r2.claim: Spending means paying zakat before death prompts a request for delay to give charity and become righteous, here glossed as performing pilgrimage; anyone falling short in zakat or pilgrimage asks to return at death.

JISHUMI:v10p6945/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6945/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v10p6945/r1.claim: Abu Amr reads fa-aṣaddaq wa-akūn with a waw and open nūn as a response to the wish or question introduced by fa; he says the waw was omitted from the codex for brevity.

JISHUMI:v10p6945/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6945/r2.speaker: الفراء
JISHUMI:v10p6945/r2.claim: Al-Farraʾ reports seeing a form in some of Ibn Masud's codices, while Ubayy's and Ibn Masud's recitation is also reported with wa-akūn.

JISHUMI:v10p6945/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6945/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6945/r3.claim: Most readers use wa-akun in the jussive, coordinated to the underlying position of fa-aṣaddaq before fa; it could also be parsed as a response to the command.

JISHUMI:v10p6945/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6945/r4.speaker: أبو عبيد
JISHUMI:v10p6945/r4.claim: Abu Ubayd prefers the jussive because the written codices omit waw, most readers use it, and coordination to the pre-fa subjunctive is grammatically sound; a cited line supports this syntax.

JISHUMI:v10p6945/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6945/r5.speaker: الفراء
JISHUMI:v10p6945/r5.claim: Al-Farraʾ reports a form in some of Abdullah ibn Masud's codices.

JISHUMI:v10p6945/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6945/r6.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
JISHUMI:v10p6945/r6.claim: The poet's line uses alhā to mean distracted or diverted from an affair.

JISHUMI:v10p6945/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6945/r7.speaker: كعب بن زهير
JISHUMI:v10p6945/r7.claim: Kaʿb's line uses lā ulhiyannaka to mean I will not distract you, despite being occupied elsewhere.

JISHUMI:v10p6946/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r1.claim: Aḥadakum is accusative as the object of the verb yāti, although death is what comes; fa-aṣaddaq is subjunctive after a wish or question introduced by fa.

JISHUMI:v10p6946/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r10.claim: The dying person asks for a brief extension after seeing signs of the afterlife, hoping to make up what was neglected.

JISHUMI:v10p6946/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r11.claim: Lawlā may be an extra particle expressing a wish for delay or may mean halā as an interrogative request for more time.

JISHUMI:v10p6946/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r12.claim: No warning against neglecting God's due is stronger than this passage.

JISHUMI:v10p6946/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r13.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r13.claim: For the view that the verse concerns hypocrites, the requested righteous standing means being among sincere believers.

JISHUMI:v10p6946/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r14.claim: For the view that it concerns believers, ṣāliḥīn means those obedient to God; Ibn Abbas also says a person who dies able to perform Hajj but has not done so, or has not paid zakat, will ask to return.

JISHUMI:v10p6946/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r15.claim: Ibn Abbas challenged those who said only disbelievers seek return after death, citing this verse about a person who failed to pay zakat or perform able-bodied Hajj.

JISHUMI:v10p6946/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r16.speaker: الضحاك
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r16.claim: Al-Dahhak reports that anyone dying without Hajj or zakat wishes for a short reprieve, but the request is denied.

JISHUMI:v10p6946/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r2.speaker: عمرو بن معدي كرب
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r2.claim: His line illustrates a subjunctive verb after an imperative: leave me so I may go aside alone.

JISHUMI:v10p6946/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r3.speaker: مقاتل وجماعة
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r3.claim: One report says the verse was revealed about hypocrites; the address calls them believers outwardly, and ṣāliḥīn means sincere believers.

JISHUMI:v10p6946/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وجماعة
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r4.claim: Another report places the revelation among believers and takes ṣāliḥīn to mean righteous deeds.

JISHUMI:v10p6946/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r9.claim: Spending is explained as spending in jihad or in charitable causes, including zakat and all other obligatory dues.

JISHUMI:v10p6948/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6948/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6948/r5.claim: The command to spend shows that wealth carries a due that must be paid before regret comes.

JISHUMI:v10p6948/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6948/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6948/r6.claim: Provision cannot be unlawful, since spending from unlawful wealth is forbidden.

JISHUMI:v10p6948/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6948/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6948/r7.claim: Their request to return so they can give charity shows their acts belong to them; otherwise the request would make no sense, and they are capable of doing them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p134/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p134/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p134/r3.claim: The commanded spending means zakat on wealth.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p134/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p134/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p134/r4.claim: At death a person asks for a short reprieve to give charity and become righteous, meaning a believer.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p134/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p134/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p134/r5.claim: The phrase may express a wish, with لا treated as extra.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p134/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p134/r6.speaker: مقاتل وجماعة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p134/r6.claim: One view says the verse concerns hypocrites; another says believers. Righteousness here may mean pilgrimage; Ibn ʿAbbās says one who dies owing zakat and able to perform Hajj asks to return.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p134/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p134/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p134/r7.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads وأكون with wāw and subjunctive as a response to the wish; others read jussive وأكن, coordinated with فأصدق and written without wāw.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546#2/r1.claim: A report promises freedom from hypocrisy for whoever recites Surat al-Munafiqun.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r1.claim: The مِن in مما رزقناكم is partitive; the required spending is intended.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r10.claim: The reading وأكن joins the jussive to the grammatical position of فأصدق, meaning ‘if delayed, I would give and become’; وأكون instead follows the overt form.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r11.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r11.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr reads وأكون as if the speaker promises, ‘and I shall be’ righteous.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r2.claim: The warning applies before death's signs become unmistakable, when one can no longer hope for respite, give acceptably, or avoid regret over withheld charity.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas urges charity before death's authority arrives, when a capable person will not be accepted.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas urges anyone with wealth to pay zakah and anyone able to perform pilgrimage to do so before death; a request to return will then be refused.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the passage concerns those withholding zakah; he argues that a person who had seen good would not seek to return, and identifies believers as its addressees.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r6.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r6.claim: Al-Hasan likewise says anyone who failed to give zakah, fast, or perform pilgrimage will ask to return at death.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r7.speaker: عكرمة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r7.claim: Ikrima says the verse was revealed concerning the people of the qibla.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r8.claim: The variant أخرتن means ‘Why did You not delay my death?’; a nearby term means a short period.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r9.speaker: أبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r9.claim: Ubayy reads فأتصدق, preserving the fuller form of the verb.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#2/r3.speaker: جمهور من المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#2/r3.claim: Most interpreters take the command to spend as referring specifically to zakāt; others read it broadly to include obligatory and recommended giving.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#2/r4.claim: The coming of death means its signs and first stages; the plea asks for another chance and reprieve.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#3/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#3/r1.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's codex reads ākhartan without the final yāʾ; the requested term is called near because it is coming and is sought only to do good deeds.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says becoming one of the righteous means pilgrimage; he says people who neglect zakāt and pilgrimage seek a return at death, despite a listener's objection.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#3/r3.claim: Most read wa-akun in the jussive: Abū ʿAlī coordinates to the implied conditional slot, while Sībawayh's account from al-Khalīl jussives it by the condition implied in the wish, without a syntactic slot.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#3/r4.speaker: أبو حاتم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#3/r4.claim: Abū Ḥātim reports a subjunctive wa-akūna coordinated with fa-atasaddaq; he notes the omitted wāw in the codex and Abū ʿAlī prefers this reading.

TABRISI:63:11#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:63:11#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:63:11#2/r10.claim: Another view says it addresses believers, and ‘righteous’ means obedient people; Ibn Abbas says anyone who died with wealth but withheld zakat or could make pilgrimage but failed would ask to return, and here ‘righteousness’ means pilgrimage.

TABRISI:63:11#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:63:11#2/r11.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:63:11#2/r11.claim: The explanation that ‘righteous’ means pilgrimage is also transmitted from Abu Abdillah.

TABRISI:63:11#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:63:11#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:63:11#2/r7.claim: Spend in good causes before death, including zakat and all other obligatory rights; death's signs prompt a futile wish for a short reprieve to give and become righteous.

TABRISI:63:11#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:63:11#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:63:11#2/r8.claim: The verse is the strongest warning against neglecting God's rights; ‘righteous’ can mean those who perform good deeds.

TABRISI:63:11#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:63:11#2/r9.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:63:11#2/r9.claim: One view says the verse addresses hypocrites.

TABRISI:63:11/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:63:11/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
TABRISI:63:11/r1.claim: Abu Amr reads ‘and I would be’ with the subjunctive; the other readers use the jussive form.

TABRISI:63:11/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:63:11/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:63:11/r3.claim: The jussive ‘and I be’ coordinates with the implied jussive condition after ‘if only you delayed me’; the request implies ‘if you delay me, I will give charity.’

TABRISI:63:11/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:63:11/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:63:11/r4.claim: Abu Amr follows the visible subjunctive after the fāʾ, a preferable construction because the overt form is clear and close; a codex of Ubayy reportedly has both verbs in that form.

TABRISI:63:11/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:63:11/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:63:11/r5.claim: The jussive can follow a conditional answer whose fāʾ and following words are understood, as in the cited Quranic parallel and two poetic examples.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r1.claim: The spending commanded here is the zakat due on one's wealth.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r2.claim: It means financial duties such as zakat and pilgrimage; on this and the previous obligatory view, the command is binding.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r3.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r3.claim: It means voluntary charity, making the command recommendatory rather than obligatory.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r4.claim: The request to be delayed means before a dying person sees what makes death certain.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r5.claim: He explains fa-aṣṣaddaq as subjunctive because a response introduced by faʾ after a question is put in the subjunctive.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r6.claim: He reads wa-akūna with wāw and a subjunctive nūn; he explains its omission in the written form as orthographic abbreviation.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r7.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads wa-akūna with the wāw, while the other readers read akunna without it.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r8.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r8.claim: With wa-akūna, the verb follows fa-aṣṣaddaq in form; with jussive akunna, it follows the syntactic position of fa-aṣṣaddaq, since the meaning is if You delay me, I will give and be righteous.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r9.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#3/r9.claim: The speaker would purify his wealth and join the believers on pilgrimage.

RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r10.claim: The appeal for more time comes when death's signs appear; the person asks to be returned to life long enough to give charity and purify himself.

RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the request to return shows these people were not believers, since a believer does not ask to return.

RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r12.speaker: الضحاك
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r12.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says anyone who dies without having performed pilgrimage or paid zakat asks to be returned, citing this verse.

RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r13.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r13.claim: Al-Kashshāf places the appeal before the dying person sees the signs that end hope of delay, constrict the throat, and make spending impossible.

RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās paraphrases the command as giving charity before death arrives, when repentance is no longer accepted and deeds no longer benefit.

RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the promised righteous conduct as performing pilgrimage.

RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r16.claim: The readings and parsing differ: fa-akūna follows fa-aṣṣaddaq; al-Mubarrad makes akuna coordinate with the subjunctive answer to the wished-for question, while Ubayy reads fa-ataṣaddaq in the original form and coordinates akuna by position.

RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes the commanded spending as zakat; another view says it is obligatory expenditure generally.

RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r1.speaker: سيبويه
RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r1.claim: Sībawayh cites poetry for coordinating a word by its syntactic position; the line addressed to Muʿāwiya uses the accusative al-ḥadīda after a preposition whose meaning is only confirmatory.

RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r2.speaker: ابن أبي سلمى
RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r2.claim: Ibn Abī Salmā's poem illustrates coordination by understood meaning: sābiqan follows the meaning of mudrikin, as if the phrase were bi-mudrikin.

RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r4.claim: The warning about wealth and children calls for remembrance before death; the order to spend calls for gratitude for what God provided.

QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11#2/r1.claim: He says this verse is especially severe for monotheists, since no one with good in the afterlife wishes to return or have life extended; Qurtubi excepts a martyr who longs to return after seeing the honor.

QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r1.claim: The command to spend before death shows that zakat must be paid promptly and may not be delayed; the same applies to other duties once their time is fixed.

QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r10.claim: The other readers put wa-akun in the jussive, coordinating with the underlying grammatical position because aṣṣaddaqa would be jussive without the fāʾ.

QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r2.claim: The dying person asks to return to worldly life to do righteous deeds.

QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk transmits Ibn ʿAbbās's view that someone able to afford Hajj or owing zakat who fails to perform it will request return at death.

QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r4.claim: When challenged that only disbelievers request return, Ibn ʿAbbās cites this passage; he says zakat becomes due at 200 and Hajj requires provisions and a mount.

QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r5.speaker: الحليمي
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r5.claim: Al-Ḥalīmī presents the saying about a person with means for Hajj asking to return as a Prophetic report, which Qurtubi says was previously given in Āl ʿImrān.

QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r6.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r6.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says Ibn ʿAbbās applies the verse to obligatory, not voluntary, spending; the zakat interpretation and amount are sound, but Hajj application depends on whether it is immediately due or may be delayed, and the means test is disputed.

QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r7.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r7.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī concludes that return and threatened punishment concern agreed obligations, so the verse covers obligatory spending through consensus or Quranic text, not voluntary giving.

QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r8.claim: Lawlā means “why not?” as a question, or lā is extra and the phrase expresses a wish; fa-aṣṣaddaqa is subjunctive after the optative particle.

QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن محيصن ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11/r9.claim: They read wa-akun in the accusative, coordinated with fa-aṣṣaddaqa.

BAYDAWI-FULL:63:8-10/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:63:8-10/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:63:8-10/r4.claim: Give some of God’s provision now to store reward for the afterlife; at death a person will ask for a short reprieve to give alms and become righteous by making amends.

BAYDAWI-FULL:63:8-10/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:63:8-10/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:63:8-10/r5.claim: The jussive أكن coordinates with the syntactic position after فاء; Abū ʿAmr reads وأكون in the subjunctive with فأصدق, while a nominative reading promises future righteousness.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p250/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p250/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p250/r1.claim: The required spending is obligatory charity from part of God's provision, before death's signs make further delay impossible.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p250/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p250/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p250/r2.claim: The verse may address believers or hypocrites; the request is for a short reprieve to give charity and become righteous believers.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p250/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p250/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p250/r3.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads “and I become” with accusative, coordinated to the preceding form; jussive connects it to the conditional meaning “if You delay me, I will give.”

QASHANI:63:9-11/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:63:9-11/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:63:9-11/r2.claim: Giving while healthy and still needing wealth builds generosity and detachment; spending only benefits when it arises from a settled disposition of liberality.

QASHANI:63:9-11/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:63:9-11/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:63:9-11/r3.claim: At death, wealth belongs to heirs, so last-minute giving yields only regret; sincere belief recognizes death as necessary at its appointed time and cannot expect delay.

QASHANI:63:9-11/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:63:9-11/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:63:9-11/r4.claim: God knows intentions, so a dying person’s promised charity is futile when it comes from miserliness and love of money rather than generosity; such wishes are lies, as another verse says.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r5.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r5.claim: Most interpret spending as zakat; another view includes required and voluntary charity. Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse concerns those withholding alms and addresses believers.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r6.claim: لولا أخرتني means “why did You not delay me?” briefly so the dying person can give charity and become righteous.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r7.claim: Most read فأصدق in the subjunctive after the wish; some read فأتصدق. Most make وأكن jussive, while al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya coordinate it with فأصدق by position.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r8.claim: Coordination by position has an absent governor with a remaining syntactic position; coordination by supposition has an absent governor with its effect remaining.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r9.claim: Several readers use subjunctive وأكون; ʿUbayd b. ʿUmayr reads it independently as a promise of righteousness.

SAMIN-DURR:63:10#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:63:10#2/r1.speaker: امرؤ القيس
SAMIN-DURR:63:10#2/r1.claim: Imru al-Qays's poem illustrates assumed genitive: منضج is treated as if annexed to صفيف, so قدير is then genitive by coordination with صفيف.

SAMIN-DURR:63:10#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:63:10#2/r2.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
SAMIN-DURR:63:10#2/r2.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr reads وأكون in the indicative as a new clause, أنا أكون, pledging himself to become righteous.

SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r1.claim: Abu Amr reads وأكون in the subjunctive, coordinating it with فأصدق, itself subjunctive as the response to the wish لولا أخرتني.

SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r2.speaker: الباقون
SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r2.claim: The other readers use jussive وأكن, deleting wāw where two consonants meet.

SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari coordinates the jussive with the syntactic position of فأصدق, as if the delayed wish yielded two promises.

SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya likewise coordinates by syntactic position and attributes this analysis to Abu Ali al-Farisi, distinguishing it from Sibawayh's implied-condition account.

SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r5.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r5.claim: Sibawayh's well-known analysis makes وأكن jussive by presuming the condition implied by the wish; Ibn Atiyya says positional coordination requires an overt condition, as at 7:186.

SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r6.claim: The author dislikes describing a Quranic inflection as assumption because the expression sounds ugly.

SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r7.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r7.claim: The Shaykh distinguishes position-based coordination, where a governing factor exists without its case effect, from assumed coordination, where the factor is absent but its effect remains.

SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r8.claim: The author illustrates the distinction with ضارب زيد وعمرا and says the present verse has no jussive governor but retains its effect; Zuhayr's verse is clearer because the absent bāʾ leaves a genitive trace.

SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r9.speaker: أبو عبيد
SAMIN-DURR:63:10/r9.claim: Abu Ubayd says the Uthmanic codex wrote وأكن without wāw.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p133/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p133/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p133/r2.claim: They should spend in obedience before death, since every negligent person regrets at death and asks for even a brief reprieve to make up what was missed, too late.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p133/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p133/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p133/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says someone with means for Hajj or liable zakat who neglects it will ask to return at death; he gives two hundred as the zakat threshold and provisions plus a mount for Hajj.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r1.speaker: بعض العارفين
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r1.claim: A gnostic says God inspires the servant at birth that life and the self are a trust, then asks at death whether the trust was kept.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r2.claim: Assimilation in the verbal form may signal that charity is concealed, or it may abbreviate speech because the dying person has no time.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r3.claim: Most readers other than Abū ʿAmr read “wa-akun” in the jussive, linked to an implied conditional: if granted time, the speaker would give charity.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r4.speaker: الخليل
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r4.claim: Sībawayh transmits from al-Khalīl that the jussive follows the position of an implied conditional, even though no explicit conditional particle appears.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r5.claim: Other grammarians explain that lawlā combines exhortation and conditional meaning, allowing the answer to be jussive by syntax or position.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r6.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads “wa-akūna” in the accusative, attaching it to the apparent wording of the response to the wish expressed by lawlā.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r7.claim: The written omission of wāw does not invalidate Abū ʿAmr’s reading, which treats it as abbreviation and fits the rule that a reading agree with the consonantal text at least potentially.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p615/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615/r1.claim: Spend from what God provided, whether obligatory or voluntary, even if the amount is small.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p615/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615/r2.claim: Believers should prepare for death before it arrives; each passing moment is already a sign and reminder of its approach.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p615/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615/r3.claim: The dying person’s request for a brief extension exposes regret and the wish to make up missed charity and prepare for the long journey.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p615/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615/r4.speaker: بعض العارفين
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615/r4.claim: Al-Ghazālī transmits from an unnamed gnostic that the Angel of Death tells a person only an hour remains, prompting a futile plea for a day to repent and give charity.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p615/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615/r5.speaker: بعض العارفين
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615/r5.claim: The report says the door of repentance closes as death throes begin; the soul’s end is either faith and a good ending or doubt and an evil ending, by prior decree.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p615/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615/r6.claim: Delaying repentance risks sins becoming an indelible seal on the heart or sudden illness and death leaving no time to cleanse it.

DURR-FULL:v8p179/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r2.claim: The Prophet says a person able to perform pilgrimage or owing zakat who neglects it will ask to return at death; Ibn Abbas supports the warning by reciting the whole surah.

DURR-FULL:v8p179/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says a dying believer who withheld zakat, pilgrimage dues, or another due to God will ask to return and give charity and zakat; God will not delay the appointed term.

DURR-FULL:v8p179/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r4.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says remembrance means the five prayers, while spending from one's provision means zakat and expenditure for pilgrimage.

DURR-FULL:v8p179/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses fa-aṣṣaddaq as paying zakat and being among the righteous as performing pilgrimage.

DURR-FULL:v8p179/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r7.speaker: الحسن عن عاصم
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r7.claim: Al-Hasan reports Asim's recitation of wa-aku and interprets the requested righteous deed as pilgrimage.

DURR-FULL:v8p180/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p180/r1.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
DURR-FULL:v8p180/r1.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit says Quranic reading is a transmitted Sunnah, so people should recite as taught; he cites the readings in Ta-Ha and this verse.

BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r1.claim: Fa-aṣṣaddaq has a first-person hamza, a doubled ṣād from assimilating the original tāʾ, and an accusative ending after an implicit particle following the wish; wa-akun is jussive, coordinated with its syntactic position.

BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r2.claim: The inward lesson links charity with righteousness and withholding with corruption; charity is for the needy out of compassion, while gifts are for beloved people out of affection.

BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r3.claim: The Prophet accepted gifts but not obligatory or voluntary charity.

BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says one who owes zakat or can afford pilgrimage will ask to return at death; he recited this verse when challenged that only disbelievers ask, and set thresholds of 200 dirhams or provision and a mount.

BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r5.claim: The verse addresses believers and Muslims, though it reproaches disbelievers too; every negligent person may wish to return.

BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r6.speaker: بعض العلماء
BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r6.claim: Some scholars infer immediate zakat and other duties because death may come any time; the author suggests prompt action is generally recommended.

BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r7.claim: Some jurists chose prayer’s earliest time to hasten toward God’s pleasure, since a person may not live to its end.

BURSEVI:v9p437/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p437/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p437/r6.claim: ‘Spend from what We provided’ means some of God’s gracious provision, not something acquired by the recipients’ own power, saved for the hereafter; the apparent command is obligatory, though broader spending better fits the context.

BURSEVI:v9p437/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p437/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p437/r7.claim: Death’s arrival means seeing its signs; the dying plea is either an entreaty for brief reprieve or a wish to return to the world.

BURSEVI:v9p437/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p437/r8.speaker: أبو الليث
BURSEVI:v9p437/r8.claim: Abū al-Layth glosses the plea as asking God to return the speaker to the world for a short additional time.

BURSEVI:v9p438/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p438/r6.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v9p438/r6.claim: Give wealth away while healthy and still needing it: spending benefits when it expresses established generosity, whereas at death wealth belongs to heirs and only regret remains.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r1.claim: Spend some of the wealth God granted before death approaches, understood as its signs and preliminaries.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes “give alms” as paying zakāt and “be among the righteous” as performing ḥajj.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r11.claim: A report through al-Tirmidhī, Ibn Jarīr, and al-Ṭabarānī attributes to the Prophet the statement that one able to perform pilgrimage or owing zakāt who fails will ask to return at death.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r2.claim: The dying person asks for a short extension so that he can give alms.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r3.speaker: أبي، عبد الله، ابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r3.claim: Ubayy, ʿAbd Allāh, and Ibn Jubayr read fa-at ṣaddaq, spelling out “so I may give charity.”

ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r4.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي، الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r4.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī and al-Zajjāj parse the jussive wa-akun as coordinated with the syntactic position of fa-aṣṣaddaq: if delayed, I would give charity and be righteous.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r5.speaker: الخليل
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r5.claim: Al-Khalīl, as reported by Sībawayh, explains the jussive by an implied condition signaled by the wish, though al-Ālūsī likes the analysis but dislikes calling it supposition.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r6.claim: The difference between coordination to syntactic position and to an imagined condition is verbal: in the former the governor exists but its effect is absent, while in the latter the governor is absent but its effect appears.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r7.speaker: الحسن، ابن جبير، أبو رجاء، ابن أبي إسحاق، مالك بن دينار، الأعمش، ابن محيصن، عبد الله بن الحسن، أبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r7.claim: These authorities read wa-akūna in the subjunctive, an unproblematic reading after the wish.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r8.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r8.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr reads wa-akūnu in the indicative; grammarians explain it as a new nominal clause with an omitted subject, though the author questions that rationale.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r9.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117#2/r9.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the spending commanded means zakāt and expenditures for pilgrimage.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r4.speaker: الكيا
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r4.claim: Al-Kiyā uses the command to spend as evidence that zakāt must be paid immediately, without delay.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the warning against neglecting these obligations is severe because death may arrive at any time, requiring constant care.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī argues that the commands to spend, the wish for a reprieve, and God's refusal to delay refute determinism; al-Ālūsī answers that the commands do not prove freedom, the wish is no evidence, and the reply merely frustrates the wish.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the determinist debate is irrelevant to the orthodox, and none of the cited statements proves the point claimed.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p118/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118/r1.claim: A narration in al-Tirmidhī's Aḥkām al-Qurʾān is mawqūf on Ibn ʿAbbās, not raised to the Prophet.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p118/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed about someone withholding zakāt and argues that asking for return fits his own claim; al-Ālūsī notes the report is not raised to the Prophet.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p118/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118/r3.claim: If the request for delay means a return to worldly life after death, the phrase “before death comes” needs no omitted word.

ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r1.claim: True honor lies in feeding others; people who gorge themselves but withhold spending and ignore nearby needy people are merely losers.

ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r10.claim: The dying person who failed to give will beg for a brief extension so they can give charity and become righteous, then grieve over leaving without those blessings.

ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r2.claim: Elmalılı says such selfishness leads to the collapse of barriers and allows Gog and Magog to devastate the land.

ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r3.claim: He identifies refusal to spend as the root of modern communism and fascism conflicts; lower societies fight over eating others’ earnings, by force, theft, or begging.

ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r4.claim: Higher societies compete in feeding, giving, completing others’ needs, covering faults, and reaching divine ranks through service.

ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r5.claim: The angels’ highest assembly contends over expiations and degrees, while the ongoing cleansing, healing, and provision of creation reflects their work under divine commands.

ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r6.claim: Islam raises believers to angelic honor through remembrance of God and spending; acquiring wealth for this purpose is nobler than earning only for family concerns.

ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r7.claim: Believers with this aspiration avoid the humiliation of begging unless severely compelled, like the poor described in 2:273.

ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r8.claim: Earning and managing wealth or family is not forbidden; what is forbidden is forgetting God and failing to consider spending for Him.

ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r9.claim: Believers should regard their wealth as God’s provision rather than the fruit of their own ability, and therefore willingly sacrifice in His path.

ELMALILI:63:9-11/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r10.claim: The report lists elevated degrees as feeding people, spreading peace, and praying at night while others sleep.

ELMALILI:63:9-11/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r11.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r11.claim: The Prophet’s supplication asks for good deeds, avoidance of wrong, love of the poor, forgiveness and mercy, protection from a people’s trial, and love of God, His beloved, and deeds that draw near to Him.

ELMALILI:63:9-11/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r12.claim: All good deeds are done from love of God; some expiate sins and others raise rank, with feeding the needy, spreading peace, and night prayer leading the latter.

ELMALILI:63:9-11/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r13.claim: Prayer heads both the expiations and the degrees, but without almsgiving people cannot rise to the honor God bestows.

ELMALILI:63:9-11/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r14.claim: Calling zakat the bridge of Islam means it is a passage to higher degrees; after obligatory dues, voluntary charity and assistance bring the greatest nearness to God.

ELMALILI:63:9-11/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r15.claim: Believers should not only tend to wealth and family but should earn, spend in God’s path, and strive to reach a higher rank before death.

ELMALILI:63:9-11/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r7.claim: Spending from what God has provided is the second trait, alongside remembrance of God, by which believers attain honor and prepare for the resurrection and Day of Mutual Loss.

ELMALILI:63:9-11/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r8.claim: A report transmitted by Tirmidhi and others says the assembly of the highest angels debates two matters: expiations and degrees.

ELMALILI:63:9-11/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r9.claim: The report lists expiations as walking to good deeds or congregational prayer, remaining in mosques after prayers, and performing ablution well in hardship.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p250/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p250/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p250/r5.claim: The discourse turns from exposing hypocrites to urging believers not to be distracted and to spend for good and communal needs, countering the order not to support the Prophet’s followers.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p250/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p250/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p250/r6.claim: Spending must begin before death, when a person’s wish for more time to do good will be useless; the shift follows the hypocrites’ words, and wealth comes before children due to context.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r10.claim: The author cites a hadith that charity extinguishes sins as water extinguishes fire.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r6.claim: The spending command counters the hypocrites’ plot and applies both to the Prophet’s entourage and other recipients, so the sentence serves as a general conclusion.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r7.claim: “Spend” covers both obligatory and recommended giving because the imperative expresses an unqualified request shared by both.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r8.claim: “From what We provided” frames giving as gratitude: the giver spends God’s favor in the way the divine law directs.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r9.claim: Min means “some of”; this eases the command and includes fixed measures such as zakat, needs assigned by ability, cause-based expiations, and voluntary giving left to personal choice.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r1.claim: Believers should give generously while able, before death prevents spending and other righteous deeds.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r10.claim: The jussive also implies a condition: if God grants the short delay, the speaker will become righteous, combining consequence with conditionality.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r2.claim: A person sensing death may plead for delay and healing to make up good deeds; the appeal expresses hope that God may grant the request.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r3.claim: لولا is an urgent exhortation here; elsewhere it can introduce an appeal, rebuke, regret, or figurative wish.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r4.claim: Although lولا normally takes an imperfect verb, the past form intensifies the plea as if its fulfillment were certain; the following results support this reading.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r5.claim: The plea asks God urgently to postpone death briefly so the believer can make up neglected charity and good works.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r6.claim: Calling the requested term near reflects the common belief that a small request is likelier to be granted; the Qur'an reports people's customary speech.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r7.speaker: النبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r7.claim: The cited hadith warns worshippers to ask firmly for forgiveness rather than making it conditional on God's will.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r8.claim: The subjunctive فأصدق follows the request with an obligatorily omitted أن.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p253/r9.claim: The majority read وأكن jussive as a direct response to the request; the waw joins clauses, not individual verbs, so no causal fāʾ appears.

TABATABAI:63:11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:63:11/r2.speaker: رواية الفقيه
TABATABAI:63:11/r2.claim: A report glosses sadaqa as almsgiving and being among the righteous as performing pilgrimage; the author treats the latter as an allusion to one instance.

TABATABAI:63:11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:63:11/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:63:11/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says someone dying with wealth but unpaid alms, or able to perform pilgrimage but not doing so, asks to return; he identifies righteousness here with pilgrimage, a view also related from Abu Abdillah.

TABATABAI:63:9-11/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:63:9-11/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:63:9-11/r10.claim: Grammatically, fa-asaddaq is subjunctive as the answer to a wish, while akuna is jussive as a conditional result: if I give charity, I will be righteous.

TABATABAI:63:9-11/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:63:9-11/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:63:9-11/r6.claim: Spending covers every kind of charitable good, obligatory such as alms and expiations and voluntary; the wording reminds people that wealth is God's gift and remains His even when entrusted to them.

TABATABAI:63:9-11/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:63:9-11/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:63:9-11/r7.claim: Spending before death means before the period of being able to use one's wealth in God's path ends.

TABATABAI:63:9-11/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:63:9-11/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:63:9-11/r8.claim: The dying person's request for a near extension implies contentment with only enough extra time to give charity, making the request easier; every future term is near.

TABATABAI:63:9-11/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:63:9-11/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:63:9-11/r9.claim: The Prophet is cited as saying that everything yet to come is near.

ASAD-NOTES:63:9#n12/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:63:9#n12/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:63:9#n12/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to surah 2, note 4, for the related explanation.

ASAD-NOTES:63:9#n13/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:63:9#n13/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:63:9#n13/r1.claim: The phrase means asking for a postponement for a near term.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p329/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p329/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p329/r6.claim: The closing three verses warn Muslims not to let wealth and children distract from remembering God; those who fail to spend for God's cause will regret it after death, when regret is useless.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p329/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p329/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p329/r7.claim: The first section identifies worldly love as the root of hypocrisy; the second urges Muslims to guard against that same cause.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p337/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p337/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p337/r3.claim: The way to preserve remembrance and resist wealth, family, and hypocrisy is to spend God’s provision for the Hereafter before death.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p337/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p337/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p337/r4.claim: The hypocrites had clenched their fists from miserliness; when poor they had promised to give generously if enriched, then broke that promise.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p338/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p338/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p338/r1.claim: Al-Tawbah 9:75–77 recounts people who pledged charity if God enriched them, but became miserly and turned away when He fulfilled their wish.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p338/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p338/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p338/r2.claim: As punishment for their broken promise, God bolstered hypocrisy in their hearts.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p338/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p338/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p338/r3.claim: Al-Ḥadīd’s account says charitable people will be raised among the righteous, including the truthful and witnesses, with a light guiding them to Paradise.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p338/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p338/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p338/r4.claim: The commentary on al-Ḥadīd says those who withhold charity are marked by hypocrisy, lack the light that leads the righteous to Paradise, and will yearn for what they omitted.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p338/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p338/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p338/r5.claim: Grammatically, the second verb is apparently coordinated with the accusative fa-aṣṣaddaqa, but Islahi reads it as the answer to a suppressed condition: had I given charity, I would be righteous.

QIRAAT-ER:63:10:23#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:63:10:23#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:63:10:23#1/r1.claim: Subjunctive akūna with wāw coordinates with aṣṣaddaqa and resolves the standard reading's jussive anomaly.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p178/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p178/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p178/r2.claim: The author chose to discuss both verses after being asked why asaddaqu is subjunctive while akun is coordinated in the jussive; their connection warrants treating them together.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p181/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p181/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p181/r4.claim: Charity precedes being righteous because the context warns against attachment to money: charity removes wealth from hand and heart, while distraction consumes heart, time, and action.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p181/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p181/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p181/r5.claim: The pairing of remembrance with righteousness is apt because someone distracted from obligations and remembering God is not among the righteous.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p182/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p182/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p182/r1.claim: Across Quranic pairings, wealth generally precedes children because it more often occupies people or invites display and boasting; he illustrates this with three passages.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p185/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p185/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p185/r1.claim: The command to spend answers the hypocrites' instruction to their allies not to support the Messenger's companions; God tells believers to spend instead.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p185/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p185/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p185/r2.claim: The partitive min asks for only a portion of one's wealth, easing people's willingness to give, whereas asking for all wealth would provoke withholding and resentment.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p185/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p185/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p185/r3.claim: Calling wealth what God provided reminds people that He owns and granted it, making it easier to give some in obedience and overcome stinginess.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p185/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p185/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p185/r4.claim: The added min in min qabli marks the temporal starting point close to death, urging people to hurry; without it, the phrase could suggest any earlier time and room to delay.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p186/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p186/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p186/r1.claim: Because every passing hour could be the hour of death, min qabli calls for immediate repentance and spending instead of procrastination.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p186/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p186/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p186/r2.claim: Putting the person before death focuses attention on the one who must repent and spend and who will regret when death reaches him.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p186/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p186/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p186/r3.claim: Fa links the death to the request both as immediate sequence and as cause: death reveals the bad outcome and triggers instant regret; thumma delays and wa only joins.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p187/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p187/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p187/r1.claim: The immediate fa suits dropping the vocative ya: at death the speaker has no time for expendable words and rushes to his request.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p187/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p187/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p187/r2.claim: Lawla is a stronger, more urgent plea and conveys self-reproach, while law is a gentler request and can be a hopeless wish rather than a sincere appeal for return.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p187/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p187/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p187/r3.claim: The past verb after lawla marks the feared loss as already realized and intensifies the plea; a present verb could imply there is still time, as in the cited examples.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p188/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p188/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p188/r1.claim: The speaker asks for only a near, short extension to make up for what he neglected, despite having wasted time without concern for his afterlife.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p188/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p188/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p188/r2.claim: Immediate fa, the omitted vocative, emphatic lawla, and the near term all compress the request, revealing the terror of death and the desperate need for little time.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p188/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p188/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p188/r3.claim: The genuine human request benefits the speaker and averts his own harm, unlike Satan's request to live until Judgment Day so he could mislead Adam's descendants.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p189/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p189/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p189/r1.claim: The human speaker explicitly says ni because the sincere, direct request serves himself; Satan's conditional oath is not for his benefit, so his pronoun is omitted and only the kasra signals it.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p189/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p189/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p189/r2.claim: Asaddaqu is subjunctive after the causal fa, while akun is jussive as the answer to the request, with the understood condition if You delay me, I will be righteous; grammarians call this coordination by meaning or by supposition.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p190/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p190/r1.speaker: جمهور السبعة
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p190/r1.claim: Most of the Seven readers recite akun in the jussive.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p190/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p190/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p190/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari analyzes the jussive as coordinated to the syntactic position of asaddaqu, as though the speaker said: if You delay me, I will give and be righteous.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p190/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p190/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p190/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya likewise says akun coordinates to the underlying position, with the implied condition if You delay me, I will give and be righteous.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p190/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p190/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p190/r4.claim: The verse combines two meanings: asaddaqu expresses cause or purpose after fa, while akun is conditional as a response to the request, rather than simply repeating the causal construction.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p190/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p190/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p190/r5.claim: Righteousness matters more for salvation than charity: a believer without resources to donate can still enter Paradise through righteousness, of which charity is one part.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p191/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p191/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p191/r2.claim: Making righteousness a conditional commitment strengthens the promise: the speaker binds himself and takes a firm pledge, fitting the more important request.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p191/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p191/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p191/r3.claim: Charity is placed first because the passage and surrounding surah repeatedly discuss wealth, distraction, and hypocrites discouraging charitable spending.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p192/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p192/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p192/r1.claim: Asaddaqu has five syllabic units compared with six in atasaddaqu, so the shorter form suits the speaker's request for a short extension.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p192/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p192/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p192/r2.claim: The extra gemination in asaddaqu, on both sad and dal, adds emphasis and abundance to the charity, implying much giving in the brief period requested.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p192/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p192/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p192/r3.claim: The shortened form joins two contextual meanings: a brief extension and abundant charity during that brief period.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p284/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p284/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p284/r1.claim: Wealth precedes children because managing and growing it consumes time and can distract a person from family; children are more valuable since wealth serves them and is left to them.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p284/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p284/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p284/r2.claim: The sequence mirrors the next verse: after forbidding distraction by wealth, the text puts charity first, since charity releases wealth from hand and heart; remembrance then corresponds to becoming righteous.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p287/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p287/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p287/r1.claim: God's command to spend answers the hypocrites' command not to support the Messenger's companions, directly reversing their call to withhold charity.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p287/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p287/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p287/r2.claim: The partitive min asks for only some of one's wealth, easing people into giving instead of asking for everything and provoking miserliness.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p287/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p287/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p287/r3.claim: Calling the wealth what We provided reminds people that it comes from God, its true provider, making them more willing to give some of it.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p288/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p288/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p288/r1.claim: Min before death marks a time beginning near death, urging people to hasten good works because any passing hour could be their last; without min, the time could be distant.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p288/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p288/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p288/r2.claim: The object ahadakum precedes death to keep each person in focus as the one needing repentance, called to spend, and left regretting if death overtakes him.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p288/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p288/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p288/r3.claim: Fa in then he says conveys both cause and immediate sequence: death causes the plea for delay, which comes at once; thumma would imply delay and waw only conjunction.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p289/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p289/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p289/r1.claim: The urgent plea omits the vocative particle, saying Lord rather than O Lord, to save time and move straight to the request.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p289/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p289/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p289/r2.claim: Lawla is a stronger, more insistent demand than law and also expresses regret; it better fits someone urgently asking for respite than a mild request or unattainable wish.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p289/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p289/r3.speaker: author
